Christopher Columbus was born in Genoa, part of present-day Italy, in 1451. His parents’ names were Dominico Colombo and Susanna Fontanarossa. He had three brothers: Bartholomew, Giovanni, and Giacomo; and a sister named Bianchinetta. Christopher became an apprentice in his father’s wool weaving business, but he also studied mapmaking and sailing as well. results.title: BBC - History - Christopher Columbus
results.content: Christopher Columbus was born in Genoa between August and October 1451. His father was a weaver and small-time merchant. As a teenager, Christopher went to sea, travelled extensively and eventually made Portugal his base. It was here that he initially attempted to gain royal patronage for a westward voyage to the Orient - his 'enterprise of the Indies'.

results.title: Where was Christopher Columbus from?
results.content: The most widespread version and the one that appears in most textbooks is that Columbus was born in Genoa, around the year 1451. According to this hypothesis, his original name was Cristoforo Colombo, son of a weaver named Domenico Colombo. The documentation supporting this theory includes notarial records and commercial contracts that link him to maritime trade activities from a young age. [...] Among the most well-known theories is the one that claims Columbus was born in Galicia, specifically in the municipality of Poio or in Sanxenxo, in the province of Pontevedra. This theory, promoted by researchers such as Celso García de la Riega in the early 20th century, argues that the real Columbus spoke [...] One of the most striking hypotheses suggests that Christopher Columbus was Portuguese, born in Madeira or the Alentejo region. This theory is based on several elements: his long stay in Lisbon, his fluent knowledge of the Atlantic coast, and his closeness to influential figures of the Portuguese court before offering his project to the Catholic Monarchs.
